outcome: Need for cesarean section due to fetal distress or suspicious Non-Stress Test (NST)
Small for gestational age (SGA; <10% percentile birth weight)
Admission to a neonatal intensive care unit (NICU)
cohort: The study included 307 pregnant women diagnosed with isolated single umbilical artery (iSUA) compared to 650 randomly selected controls with double umbilical artery (DUA), drawn from a larger cohort of 40,800 pregnant women who underwent detailed ultrasonography.
finding: Cases with isolated single umbilical artery (iSUA) were associated with significantly lower Apgar scores, lower birth weight, higher SGA prevalence, increased need for cesarean section due to fetal distress, higher intrauterine fetal death (IUFD), and higher rates of preterm birth compared to those with double umbilical artery (DUA).
mod_finding: The iSUA group had a higher need for cesarean section due to fetal distress or suspicious non-stress tests compared to the DUA group.
